# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Apply the given Callable to the value of this instance, and return a new <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html\">ara::core</a>:: Result with the result of the call.</p><p>The Callable is expected to be compatible to one of these two interfaces: • Result<XXX, E> f(const T&); • <ARTechTerm{XXX f(const T&);}> • <ARNewline{}> • <ARNewline{}> • <ARTechTerm{Callable}> • Result<XXX> or a XXX directly, where XXX can be any type that is suitable for use by <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>.</p><p>The return type of this function is decltype(f(Value())) for a template argument F that returns a <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a> type, and it is Result<decltype(f(Value())), E> for a template argument F that does not return a <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a> type.</p><p>If this instance does not contain a value, a new Result<XXX, E> is still created and returned, with the original error contents of this instance being copied into the new instance.}>}</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n\n"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n1 Introduction\nThis document defines basic requirements that apply to all Functional Clusters of the\nAdaptive Platform.\nTo aid in this, it also defines functionality that applies to the entire framework, including\na set of common data types used by multiple Functional Clusters as part of their public\ninterfaces.\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms and abbreviations relevant to Adaptive Core\nthat are not included in the [1, AUTOSAR glossary]."

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Limitations\n•\nThe specification of some data types (Array, Map, Optional, String, StringView,\nVariant) mentions supporting constructs, but lacks a precise scope definition of\nthis term.\n•\nThe specification of some data types (Map, Vector, String) is lacking a compre-\nhensive definition of memory allocation behavior; it currently only describes it as\nimplementation-defined.\n•\nChapter 7.2 (Functional Specification) describes some behavior informally that\nshould rather be given as specification items.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nNo restrictions to applicability.\n5 Dependencies to other modules\nThis Functional Cluster only depends on [2], in particular the C++ standard library.\n10 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7 Requirements Specification\n7.1 General requirements for all Functional Clusters\nThe goal of this section is to define a common set of basic requirements that apply\nto all Functional Clusters of the Adaptive Platform. It adds a common part to the\nspecifications and it needs to be respected by platform vendors.\n[SWS_CORE_90001] Include folder structure\n⌈\nAll #include directives in header files\nthat refer to ARA libraries shall be written in the form\n#include \"ara/fc/header.h\"\nwith ara as the first path element, fc being the remaining directory path of the imple-\nmentation's\ninstalled\nheader file, starting with the Functional Cluster short name, and\nheader.h being the filename of the header file.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00116, RS_AP_00111)\nThe Functional Cluster short names are defined in [3].\nExample: Execution Management (short name exec) provides class\nExecution-\nClient\n, which can be accessed with:\n#include \"ara/exec/execution_client.h\"\nThe \"...\" form of #include statements shall be used, due to the recommendation given\nin [4, the C++14 standard] section 16.2.7.\n[SWS_CORE_90002] Prevent multiple inclusion of header file\n⌈\nAll public header\nfiles shall prevent multiple inclusion by using #include guards that are likely to be\nsystem-wide unique.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00111)\nWhile uniqueness can generally not be guaranteed, the likelihood of collisions can be\ndecreased with a naming scheme that is regular and results in long symbol names.\nThe following #include guard naming scheme should be used by implementations for\nall header files that cover symbols within the\nara\nnamespace or a sub-namespace\ntherein:\nARA_<PATH>_H_\nwhere <PATH> is the relative path name of the header file within the location of the\nimplementation's\ninstalled\nheader files, starting with the Functional Cluster name (and\nomitting the file extension), and with all components of <PATH> separated by under-\nscore (\"_\") characters and containing only upper-case characters of the ASCII charac-\nter set.\nExample: The header file included with\n#include \"ara/log/logger.h\"\nshould\nuse the #include guard symbol\nARA_LOG_LOGGER_H_\n.\n23 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_90003]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈\nC/C++ symbols that start with\nARA\nare reserved for\nuse by AUTOSAR.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00111)\nThe Adaptive Platform generally avoids the use of C/C++ preprocessor macros. How-\never, in case macros are introduced at some later point in time, any such macro will\nstart with the prefix\nARA\n. Platform vendors should thus not define any symbols (both\nmacros and C/C++ ones) with this prefix, lest they conflict with such future additions to\nthe standard.\n[SWS_CORE_90004]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nImplementation-defined declaration classifiers\n⌈\nAll\nAPIs shall be implemented with the exact same declaration classifiers that are speci-\nfied, except for\ninline\nand\nfriend\n, which may be added as necessary.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00111)\nNote: The order of declarations may be freely chosen.\n[4, The C++14 standard] defines in chapter 7.1 [dcl.spec] the specifiers that can be\nused in a declaration; these include, for instance,\nstatic\n,\nvirtual\n,\nconstexpr\n,\ninline\nand\nfriend\n. An implementation that uses a different set of specifiers in its\ndeclaration of a specified API may be incompatible to the standard, or may allow non-\nstandardized usage of that API, leading to portability concerns.\n7.1.1 Initialize/Deinitialize\nara::core::Initialize\nallows a central initialization of all included shared li-\nbraries of the ARA framework. This could include static initializers or the setup of\ndaemon links (details are up to the platform vendor).\nThe general advice for application developers is to call\nara::core::Initialize\nright at the entry point of the application.\n[SWS_CORE_90020]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈\nIf functionality is called that depends on prior initial-\nization via\nara::core::Initialize\nand\nara::core::Initialize\nhas not been\ncalled, the Functional Cluster implementation shall treat this as a\nViolation\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00111)\nThe rationale to treat this as a\nViolation\nis that it cannot be handled by the caller of\nthe API at the point in time where the error is detected. Aborting execution is the only\nway to signal this kind of systematic error and prevent later failures.\n24 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "source_page": 25,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7.2 Functional Specification\nThis section describes the concepts that are introduced with this Functional Cluster.\nParticular emphasis is put on error handling.\n7.2.1 Error handling\n7.2.1.1 Types of unsuccessful operations\nDuring execution of an implementation of Adaptive Platform APIs, different abnormal\nconditions might be detected and need to be handled and/or reported. Based on\ntheir nature, the following types of unsuccessful operations are distinguished within\nthe Adaptive Platform:\n[SWS_CORE_00020]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of an Error\n⌈\nAn\nError\nis the inability of\nan assumed-bug-free API function to fulfill its specified purpose; it is often a conse-\nquence of invalid and/or unexpected (i.e. possibly valid, but received in unexpected\ncircumstances) input data. An\nError\nis recoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00021]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of a Violation\n⌈\nA\nViolation\nis the con-\nsequence of failed pre- or post-conditions of internal state of the application framework.\nThey are the Adaptive Platform's analog to a failed assertion. A\nViolation\nis non-\nrecoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00022]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of a Corruption\n⌈\nA\nCorruption\nis the\nconsequence of the corruption of a system resource, e.g. stack or heap overflow, or a\nhardware memory flaw (including even, for instance, a detected bit flip). A\nCorrup-\ntion\nis non-recoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00023]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of a Failed Default Allocation\n⌈\nA\nFailed Default Allocation\nis the inability of the framework's default memory\nallocation mechanism to satisfy an allocation request. A\nFailed Default Alloca-\ntion\nis non-recoverable.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\nIt is expected that a\nViolation\nor\nCorruption\nmight occur during development of\nthe framework, when new features are just coming together, but will not be experienced\nby a user (i.e. an application developer), unless there is something seriously wrong in\nthe system's environment (e.g. faulty hardware:\nCorruption\n), or basic assumptions\nabout resource requirements are violated (\nViolation\n), or possibly the user runs the\nframework in a configuration that is not supported by its vendor (\nViolation\n).\n7.2.1.2 Traditional error handling in C and C++\nThe C language largely relies on error codes for any kind of error handling. While it\nalso has the\nsetjmp\n/\nlongjmp\nfacility for performing non-local gotos, its use for error\n25 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P26_76",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nhandling is not widespread, mostly due to the difficulty of reliably avoiding resource\nleaks.\nError codes in C come in several flavors:\n•\nreturn values\n•\nout parameters\n•\nerror singletons (e.g.\nerrno\n)\nTypically, these error codes in C are plain\nint\nvariables, making them a very low-level\nfacility without any type safety.\nC++ inherited these approaches to error handling from C (not least due to the inher-\nitance of the C standard library as part of the C++ standard), but it also introduced\nexceptions as an alternative means of error propagation. There are many advantages\nof using exceptions for error propagation, which is why the C++ standard library gen-\nerally relies on them for error propagation.\nNotwithstanding the advantages of exceptions, error codes are still in widespread use\nin C++, even within the standard library. Some of that can be explained with concerns\nabout binary compatibility with C, but many new libraries still prefer error codes to\nexceptions. Reasons for that include:\n•\nwith exceptions, it can be difficult to reason about a program's control flow\n•\nexceptions have much higher runtime cost than error codes (either in general, or\nonly in the exception-thrown case)\nThe first of these reasons concerns both humans and code analysis tools. Because\nexceptions are, in effect, a kind of hidden control flow, a C++ function that seems to\ncontain only a single\nreturn\nstatement might in fact have many additional function\nreturns due to exceptions. That can make such a function hard to review for humans,\nbut also hard to analyze for static code analysis tools.\nThe second one is even more critical in the context of developing safety-critical soft-\nware. The specification of C++ exceptions pose significant problems for C++ compiler\nvendors that want their products be certified for development of safety-critical software.\nIn fact, ASIL-certified C++ compilers generally do not support exceptions at all. One\nparticular problem with exceptions is that exception handling, as specified for C++, im-\nplies the use of dynamic memory allocation, which generally has non-predictable or\neven unbounded execution time. This makes exceptions currently unsuitable for devel-\nopment of certain safety-critical software in the automotive industry.\n7.2.1.3 Handling of unsuccessful operations in the Adaptive Platform\nThe types of unsuccessful operations defined in section 7.2.1.1 (Types of unsuccessful\noperations) are to be treated in different ways.\n26 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P27_77",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_00002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_00002] Handling of Errors\n⌈\nAn\nError\nshall be returned from the func-\ntion as an instance of\nara::core::Result\nor\nara::core::Future\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_-\n00142, RS_AP_00139, RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_CORE_00003] Handling of Violations\n⌈\nIf a\nViolation\nis detected, then the\noperation shall be terminated by either:\n•\nthrowing an exception that is not a subclass of\nara::core::Exception\n•\nexplicitly terminating the process abnormally via a call to\nara::core::Abort\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\n[SWS_CORE_00004] Handling of Corruptions\n⌈\nIf a\nCorruption\nis detected, it shall\nresult in unsuccessful process termination, in an implementation-defined way.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nAP_00142)\nNote: It can either be abnormal or normal unsuccessful termination, depending on the\nimplementation's ability to detect the\nCorruption\nand to react to it by cleaning up\nresources.\n[SWS_CORE_00005] Handling of failed default allocations\n⌈\nA \"failed default allo-\ncation\" shall be treated the same as a\nViolation\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00142)\nNote: An error of a custom allocator is not subject to this definition.\n7.2.1.4 Facilities for Error Handling\nFor handling\nErrors\n, there are a number of data types defined that help in dealing\nwith them. These are described in the following subsections.\n7.2.1.4.1 ErrorCode\nAs its name implies,\nara::core::ErrorCode\nis a form of error code; however, it\nis a class type, loosely modeled on\nstd::error_code\n, and thus allows much more\nsophisticated handling of errors than the simple error codes as used in typical C APIs.\nIt always contains a low-level\nerror code value\nand a reference to an\nerror do-\nmain\n.\nThe\nerror code value\nis an enumeration, typically a scoped one. When stored into\na\nara::core::ErrorCode\n, it is type-erased into an integral type and thus handled\nsimilarly to a C-style error code. The\nerror domain\nreference defines the context for\nwhich the\nerror code value\nis applicable and thus provides some measure of type\nsafety.\nAn\nara::core::ErrorCode\nalso contains a\nsupport data value\n, which\ncan\nbe\ndefined by an implementation of the Adaptive Platform to give a vendor-specific addi-\ntional piece of data about the error.\n27 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P28_78",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10302",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n[SWS_CORE_10302]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nSemantics of ErrorCode\n⌈\nThe type\nara::core::-\nErrorCode\nprovides a class interface for storing an error condition. It shall contain\nthese properties:\n•\nerror code value: an integral representation of a low-level error code\n•\nerror domain: reference to the context for which the\nerror code value\nis applicable\n•\nsupport data value: an optional vendor-specific additional piece of data about the\nerror\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119)\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances are usually not created directly, but only via the\nforwarding form of the function\nara::core::Result::FromError\n.\nAn\nara::core::ErrorCode\nis not restricted to any known set of error domains.\nIts internal type erasure of the enumeration makes sure that it is a simple (i.e., non-\ntemplated) type which can contain arbitrary errors from arbitrary domains.\nHowever, comparison of two\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances only considers the\nerror code value\nand the\nerror domain\nreference; the\nsupport data value\nmember is not considered for checking equality. This is due to the way\nara::core:-\n:ErrorCode\ninstances are usually compared against a known set of errors for which\nto check:\n1\nErrorCode ec = ...\n2\nif (ec == MyEnum::some_error)\n3\n// ...\n4\nelse if (ec == AnotherEnum::another_error)\n5\n// ...\nEach of these comparisons will create a temporary\nara::core::ErrorCode\nobject\nfor the right-hand side of the comparison, and then compare\nec\nagainst that. Such au-\ntomatically created instances naturally do not contain any meaningful\nsupport data\nvalue\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10301]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nComparison of ara::core::ErrorCode instances\n⌈\nAny comparison of two\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances shall consider only the\nfollowing members:\n•\nerror code value\n•\nerror domain\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00119)\nThis frequent creation of temporary\nara::core::ErrorCode\ninstances is expected\nto be so fast as to induce no noticeable runtime cost. This is usually ensured by\nara::core::ErrorCode\nbeing a\nliteral type\n.\n[SWS_CORE_10300]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrorCode type properties\n⌈\nClass\nara::core::-\nErrorCode\nshall be a\nliteral type\n, as defined in section 3.9-10 [basic.types] of [4, the\nC++14 standard].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n28 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P29_79",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10303",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7.2.1.4.2 ErrorDomain\nara::core::ErrorDomain\nis the abstract base class for concrete error domains\nthat are defined within Functional Clusters or even Adaptive Applications. This class is\nloosely based on\nstd::error_category\n, but differs significantly from it.\nAn error domain has an associated error code enumeration and an associated base\nexception type.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nto do this; either by throwing certain kinds of exceptions (if the implementation supports\nC++ exceptions), or by calling\nara::core::Abort\n.\nCalling\nara::core::Abort\nwill result in an\nExplicit Operation Abortion\n,\nwhich usually leads to an\nUnexpected Termination\nas defined by [7]. This section\ndefines the behavior of this mechanism.\nLike\nstd::abort\n, calling\nara::core::Abort\nis meant to terminate the current pro-\ncess abnormally and immediately, without performing stack unwinding and without call-\ning destructors of static objects.\n[SWS_CORE_12402]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nNoreturn property for Abort\n⌈\nThe function\nara:-\n:core::Abort\nshall not return to its caller.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_12403]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nLogging of Explicit Operation Abortion\n⌈\nCalling\nara::core::Abort\nshall result in a log message, which shall contain the string that\nhas been passed to the function as argument, being output to the process's standard\nerror stream.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_12407]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nThread-safety of Explicit Operation Abortion\n⌈\nWhile a call to\nara::core::Abort\nis in progress, other calls to this function shall\nblock the calling threads.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nara::core::Abort\nprovides a means to add a hook into the system, by calling\nara::core::SetAbortHandler\n, similar to the way\nstd::atexit\nallows to install\na callback for the\nstd::exit\nmechanism. Unlike\nstd::atexit\n, however, it is only\npossible to set exactly\none\nhandler with\nara::core::SetAbortHandler\n.\n[SWS_CORE_12404]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nAbortHandler invocation\n⌈\nCalling\nara::core::-\nAbort\nshall invoke the\nAbortHandler\n if it has been set  after the log message as\nper [SWS_CORE_12403] has been output.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.3.1 AbortHandler\nThis handler can be installed with\nara::core::SetAbortHandler\n. It is invoked in\nturn when\nara::core::Abort\nis called, and it may perform arbitrary operations and\nthen has these four principal choices for its final statements: it can either\n•\nterminate the process, or\n•\nreturn from the function call, or\n•\ndefer function return by entering an infinite loop, or\n•\nperform a non-local goto operation such as\nstd::longjmp\n.\nThe use of non-local goto operations, including\nstd::longjmp\n, is strongly discour-\naged and also expressively prohibited by MISRA, the AUTOSAR C++14 Coding Guide-\nlines, and most other coding guidelines as well.\n38 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nSimilarly, deferring function return by entering an infinite loop is discouraged as well;\nwhile this still leads to the desired outcome that the\noperation\nwhich caused a\nViola-\ntion\nhas been aborted, it will do so at the cost of defunct'ing the calling thread and\nrisking the destabilization of the software, which already has encountered a\nViola-\ntion\n.\nAn\nAbortHandler\nthat terminates the process is strongly advised to do so by calling\nstd::abort\n. This will make sure that the\nUnexpected Termination\nis properly\nseen by Execution Management as an\nAbnormal Termination\nas well.\nIf the\nAbortHandler\nreturns, or if no\nAbortHandler\nis defined at all, then the final\naction of\nara::core::Abort\nis to call\nstd::abort\n.\n[SWS_CORE_12405]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nFinal action without AbortHandler\n⌈\nIf there is no\ncustom\nara::core::AbortHandler\nthat has been installed with\nara::core:-\n:SetAbortHandler\n, then the implementation of\nara::core::Abort\nshall call\nstd::abort()\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_12406]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nFinal action with a returning AbortHandler\n⌈\nIf there\nis a custom\nara::core::AbortHandler\nthat has been installed with\nara::core:-\n:SetAbortHandler\nand it returns, then the implementation of\nara::core::Abort\nshall call\nstd::abort()\n.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.3.2 SIGABRT handler\nIn addition to the\nara::core::AbortHandler\n, or alternatively to it, the application\ncan also influence this mechanism by installing a signal handler for SIGABRT.\nThe signal handler for SIGABRT has the same choices of actions as the\nara::core:-\n:AbortHandler\n: it can terminate the process, return from the function call, defer\nfunction return by entering an infinite loop, or perform a non-local goto operation. The\nsame caveats as for the\nara::core::AbortHandler\napply here: non-local goto\noperations and infinite loops should be avoided.\nIf the SIGABRT handler does not return, it should in general terminate abnormally\nwith SIGABRT. To do this without entering an infinite loop, it should restore the default\ndisposition of SIGABRT with\nstd::signal(SIGABRT, SIG_DFL)\nand then re-raise\nSIGABRT with e.g.\nstd::raise(SIGABORT)\n.\nThis second step of influence that the SIGABRT handler provides allows applications\nthat are already handling other synchronous signals such as SIGSEGV or SIGFPE to\ntreat SIGABRT the same way.\n39 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n7.2.4 Advanced data types\n7.2.4.1 AUTOSAR types\n7.2.4.1.1 InstanceSpecifier\nInstances of\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nare used to identify service port\nprototype instances within the AUTOSAR meta-model and are therefore used in the\nara::com\nAPI and elsewhere. A detailed description and background can be found\nin [8] sections 6.1 (Instance Identifiers) and 9.4.4 (Usage of meta-model identifiers\nwithin ara::com based application code).\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\ncan conceptually be understood to be a wrapper\nfor a string representation of a valid meta-model path. It is designed to be either con-\nstructed from a string representation via a factory method\nara::core::Instance-\nSpecifier::Create\n, which provides an exception-free solution, or directly by using\nthe constructor, which might throw an exception if the string representation is invalid.\n[SWS_CORE_10200] Valid InstanceSpecifier representations\n⌈\nThe content of a\nvalid\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nconsists of a \"/\"-separated list of model el-\nement names starting from an\nExecutable\nto the respective\nPortPrototype\nto\nwhich the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nshall apply.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10201] Validation of meta-model paths\n⌈\nThe construction mech-\nanisms of class\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nshall reject meta-model\npaths that are syntactically invalid according to the syntax rules defined in\n[SWS_CORE_10200].\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n[SWS_CORE_10202] Construction of InstanceSpecifier objects\n⌈\nAPIs for con-\nstruction of\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nobjects shall be available in both\npotentially-throwing and non-throwing form.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.4.1.2 ScaleLinearAndTexttable\nA\nara::core::ScaleLinearAndTexttable\ntype is a struct type that emulates an\nenumeration type with extended capabilities, such as those given in [9, the C++17\nstandard]\nIn particular, it can hold the values of the enumeration, but also any value of the under-\nlying type of the Enumeration Data Type with which it was defined.\n7.2.4.2 Types derived from the base C++ standard\nIn addition to AUTOSAR-devised data types, which are mentioned in the previous sec-\ntions, the Adaptive Platform also contains a number of generic data types and helper\nfunctions.\n40 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nSome types are already contained in [4, the C++14 standard]; however, types with al-\nmost identical behavior are re-defined within the\nara::core\nnamespace. The reason\nfor this is that the memory allocation behavior of the\nstd::\ntypes is often unsuitable\nfor automotive purposes. Thus, the\nara::core\nones define their own memory allo-\ncation behavior, and perform some other necessary adaptions as well, including about\nthe throwing of exceptions.\n[SWS_CORE_00040]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nErrors originating from C++ standard classes\n⌈\nFor\nthe classes in ara::core specified below in terms of the corresponding classes of the\nC++ standard, all functions that are specified by [4, the C++14 standard], [9, the C++17\nstandard], or [10, the draft C++20 standard] to throw any exceptions, are instead spec-\nified to be the cause of a\nViolation\nwhen they do so.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\nExamples for such data types are: Array, Vector, Map, and String.\n7.2.4.2.1 Array\nThis section describes the\nara::core::Array\ntype that represents a container\nwhich encapsulates fixed size arrays.\nara::core::Array\nis an almost-equivalent of\nstd::array\n, and most type proper-\nties of\nstd::array\napply to\nara::core::Array\nas well.\nThese differences to\nstd::array\nare intended:\n•\nstd::array::at\nhas been omitted (in order to avoid mandatory exception han-\ndling)\n[SWS_CORE_11200] Array base behavior\n⌈\nara::core::Array\nand all its member\nfunctions and supporting constructs shall behave identical to those of header\n<array>\nfrom [4, the C++14 standard], except for the differences specified in this document.\n⌋\n(RS_AP_00130)\n7.2.4.2.2 SteadyClock\n7.2.4.2.2.1 Definitions of terms\nThe C++\nstd::chrono\nlibrary defines a number of concepts and types for handling\ntime and durations. One of these concepts is that of a clock which is able to create\nsnapshots of specific time points. When talking about clocks and time points, the\nthree qualities\nresolution\n,\nprecision\n, and\naccuracy\nare distinguished within this docu-\nment as follows:\n•\nThe\nresolution\nrelates to the smallest increment that can be expressed with\nthe clock's measurement data type.\n41 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "source_page": 42,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nFor clocks of the POSIX\nclock_gettime\nAPI, the\nresolution\nis implicitly de-\nfined as nanoseconds by the API's usage of\nstruct timespec\nwith its\ntime-\nspec::tv_nsec\nfield.\nFor C++ clocks of the\nstd::chrono\nAPIs, the\nresolution\nis variable.\n•\nThe\nprecision\nof a clock is the smallest time interval that its timer is able to\nmeasure. The\nprecision\nis implementation-defined and depends on the prop-\nerties and capabilities of the physical machine as well as the operating system.\n•\nThe\naccuracy\nof a clock is the relation between the reported value and the truth.\nIn addition to that, the\nepoch\nis an important property of a clock as well, as it defines\nthe base of the time range that can originate from a clock. Clocks that measure cal-\nendar time often use Unix time, which is given as number of seconds (without leap\nseconds) since the Unix Epoch, which is 1970-01-01, 00:00:00 UTC.\nClocks that place more emphasis on high\nprecision\noften do not relate to calendar\ntime at all, but generate timestamps as offsets from something like the power-up time\nof the system.\n7.2.4.2.2.2 Clocks in the Adaptive Platform\nThe C++\nstd::chrono\nlibrary defines a number of standard clocks. Amongst these\nis\nstd::chrono::steady_clock\n, which represents a monotonic clock whose time\npoints are strictly increasing with a fixed interval.\nHowever, the C++ standard does not place any requirements on the\nresolution\n,\nprecision\n, and\naccuracy\nof this clock. The undefinedness of its\nresolution\ncan\npose some difficulties for application programmers, but these can usually be solved\nby agreeing on a common  or minimum \nresolution\n. The\nprecision\nand\nac-\ncuracy\nare always dependent on the physical properties of the machine and of the\noperating system.\nThe Adaptive Platform defines\nara::core::SteadyClock\nas a\nstd::chrono\n-\ncompatible clock with nanosecond\nresolution\nand a\nstd::int64_t\ndatatype. Its\nprecision\nand\naccuracy\nare still implementation-defined and can be given as char-\nacteristic values of a concrete platform. Its\nepoch\nis the power-up time of the ECU.\nWith these properties, timestamps generated by\nara::core::SteadyClock\nwill not\noverflow until 292 years after its\nepoch\n.\nIt is the standard clock of the Adaptive Platform and should be used for most timekeep-\ning purposes.\nThe properties of\nara::core::SteadyClock\nimply that a type alias to\nstd::chrono::steady_clock\nis a conforming implementation of\nara::core:-\n:SteadyClock\n, if\nstd::chrono::steady_clock::period\nis equivalent to\nstd::nano\n, and\nstd::chrono::steady_clock::rep\nis a 64-bit signed integer\ntype such as\nstd::int64_t\n.\n42 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n•\ninitialization of ARA framework specific data structures\n•\ninitialization of system resources\n•\nspawning of background threads\n⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\n[SWS_CORE_15004]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng\nShutdown and de-initialization of ARA\n⌈\nThe\nara:-\n:core::Deinitialize\nfunction shall initiate the shutdown of the ARA framework,\nwhich might include (but is not limited to):\n•\norderly shutdown of spawned background threads\n•\ndeallocation of dynamically allocated memory\n•\ndeallocation of other system resources\n⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\nAn error returned by\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis the only way for the ARA to re-\nport an error that is guaranteed to be available, e.g. in case\nara::log\nhas already\nbeen deinitialized.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\n8.1.19 Initialization and Shutdown\nThis section describes the global initialization and shutdown functions that initialize\nresp. deinitialize data structures and threads of the AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive\nApplications.\n[SWS_CORE_10001]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_812",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "(Pre-)Initialization of the ARA Framework.\nPrior to this call, interaction with the ARA is not allowed with the exception of types intended to\nbe used independently of initialization: ara::core::ErrorCode, ara::core::StringView,\nara::core::Result but not the function ValueOrThrow, ara::core::ErrorDomain and subclasses,\nbut not the function ThrowAsException. It is strongly recommended to make this call in a place\nwhere it is guaranteed that static initialization has completed."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_813",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_Main_00011)\n[SWS_CORE_10002]\n⌊\nDRAFT\ng ⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_core_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P182_814",
      "source_element": "SWS_CORE_10001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core",
      "source_page": 182,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Shutdown of the ARA Framework.\nAfter this call, no interaction with the ARA is allowed with the exception of types intendent to be\nused independently of initialization: ara::core::ErrorCode, ara::core::StringView,\nara::core::Result but not the function ValueOrThrow, ara::core::ErrorDomain and subclasses,\nbut not the function ThrowAsException. As a prerequisite to calling this API it is expected that\nthe use of ARA interfaces is completed (with the given exceptions). It is strongly recommended\nto make this call in a place where it is guaranteed that the static initialization has completed and\ndestruction of statically initialized data has not yet started."
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR AP R21-11\nB Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)\nB.1 Overview\nAUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between\nFunctional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which\nmight depend e.g. on the used Operating System.\nThis chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional\nClusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe\nInter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. In addition, the standardized public interfaces\nwhich are accessible by user space applications (see chapter 8 (API specification))\ncan also be used for interaction between Functional Clusters.\nThe goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and in-\nteraction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between\ndocuments specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementa-\ntion of different Functional Clusters. Details of the interfaces are up to the platform\nprovider. Additional interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.\nB.2 Interface Tables\nB.2.1 Functional Cluster initialization\nara::core::Initialize\nand\nara::core::Deinitialize\ninitialize and deini-\ntialize other Functional Clusters as necessary for the particular implementation. All\nFunctional Clusters where this is necessary thus need to provide internal interfaces for\ntheir initialization and deinitialization.\nC History of Specification Items\nPlease note that the lists in this chapter also include specification items that have been\nremoved from the specification in a later version. These specification items do not\nappear as hyperlinks in the document.\n187 of 218 Document ID 903: AUTOSAR_SWS_AdaptivePlatformCore"

  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h3>Rolle & Verwendungszweck</h3><p>Das Modul <code>ara::core</code> stellt das fundamentale Basis- und Laufzeitfundament der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform dar. Es definiert den gemeinsamen Standard für Datentypen, Fehlerbehandlungsmuster, asynchrone Kontrollflüsse und Lebenszyklusfunktionen über alle Functional Clusters sowie für anwendungsspezifischen Adaptive-Code hinweg <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00001\">[SWS_CORE_00001]</a>. Um in sicherheitskritischen automobilen Steuergeräten deterministisches Verhalten zu garantieren, ersetzt <code>ara::core</code> traditionelle C++-Mechanismen wie unkontrollierte Exception-Weitergabe oder nicht echtzeitfähige Standard-Allokatoren durch explizite Typverträge.</p><p>Die Kernaufgaben von <code>ara::core</code> umfassen:</p><ul><li><strong>Einheitliches Fehlermodell:</strong> Bereitstellung von <code>ara::core::Result<T, E></code> und <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> zur expliziten, typsicheren und ausnahmelosen Rückgabe von Fehlern im regulären Kontrollfluss.</li><li><strong>Asynchronitätsmuster:</strong> Standardisierung von <code>ara::core::Future</code> und <code>ara::core::Promise</code> als konsistente Brücke für nebenläufige und verteilte Berechnungen in allen AUTOSAR-AP-Schnittstellen.</li><li><strong>Port- und Instanzabstraktion:</strong> Bereitstellung des Typs <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code>, der logische Software-Architektur-Modellelemente auf konkrete Plattform- und Kommunikationskonfigurationen abbildet.</li><li><strong>Lebenszyklus-Initialisierung:</strong> Zentraler Einstiegspunkt über <code>Initialize()</code> und <code>Deinitialize()</code> für das Hoch- und Herunterfahren der Adaptive Platform im Anwendungsprozess.</li><li><strong>Automotive-fähige Hilfs- und Container-Typen:</strong> Typen wie <code>Span</code>, <code>StringView</code>, <code>Optional</code> und <code>Variant</code> zur ressourcenschonenden, kopierfreien Datenübergabe.</li></ul><h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3><p>Alle öffentlichen ARA-Schnittstellen (AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive Applications) basieren zwingend auf den Typverträgen von <code>ara::core</code>. Die Spezifikation unterscheidet dabei funktionale Datenstrukturen, Identifikatoren und Fehlerbehandlungsprimitive:</p><ul><li><strong>Initialisierungsvertrag:</strong> Vor dem Aufruf jeglicher funktionaler ARA-APIs muss der Prozess <code>ara::core::Initialize()</code> aufrufen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00701\">[SWS_CORE_00701]</a>. Dieser Aufruf initialisiert interne Laufzeitstrukturen, Log-Sinks und abhängige Cluster. Vor Beendigung des Prozesses ist korrespondierend <code>ara::core::Deinitialize()</code> aufzurufen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00801\">[SWS_CORE_00801]</a>.</li><li><strong>Result- und Fehlervertrag:</strong> Operationen, die fehlschlagen können, liefern ein <code>ara::core::Result<T, E></code> zurück <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00733\">[SWS_CORE_00733]</a>. Ein <code>Result</code> kapselt entweder den gewünschten Wert vom Typ <code>T</code> oder einen <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00763\">[SWS_CORE_00763]</a>. Jeder <code>ErrorCode</code> referenziert eine konkrete <code>ErrorDomain</code> mit eindeutiger 64-Bit-Kennung <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00767\">[SWS_CORE_00767]</a>, wodurch Fehlernummern clusterübergreifend kollisionsfrei interpretiert werden.</li><li><strong>Asynchroner Vertrag:</strong> Asynchrone Schnittstellen liefern ein <code>ara::core::Future<T, E></code> zurück <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00736\">[SWS_CORE_00736]</a>. Aufrufer können synchron auf das Eintreffen warten (<code>wait()</code>, <code>wait_for()</code>) oder über <code>GetResult()</code> das finale <code>Result<T, E></code> abholen, ohne dass C++-Standardausnahmen geworfen werden.</li><li><strong>Instanzbindung:</strong> Der <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> kapselt einen qualifizierten Manifest-Pfad (z. B. <code>/Executable/PortPrototype</code>) als eindeutigen Schlüssel zur Konfigurationsauflösung <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_08001\">[SWS_CORE_08001]</a>.</li><li><strong>Forwarding-Header:</strong> Der Namensraum <code>ara</code> ist für AUTOSAR reserviert. Um Compile-Zeiten zu optimieren und modulare Abhängigkeiten zu trennen, stellt jeder Cluster Forwarding-Header <code><fc>_fwd.h</code> bereit.</li></ul><h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3><p>Der Lebenszyklus einer Adaptive Application beginnt typischerweise mit dem Aufruf von <code>Initialize()</code>. Anschließend werden funktionale Cluster wie <code>ara::com</code>, <code>ara::exec</code> oder <code>ara::diag</code> verwendet, wobei asynchrone Schnittstellen durch das Zusammenspiel von <code>Promise</code> und <code>Future</code> synchronisiert werden. B. Timeout, temporäre Nichtverfügbarkeit eines Dienstes oder ungültige Nutzereingaben). Sie werden über <code>Result<T, E></code> an den Aufrufer übergeben und müssen von der Fachlogik ausgewertet und behandelt werden <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00021\">[SWS_CORE_00021]</a>.</li><li><strong>Unbehebbare Regelverletzungen (Violations):</strong> Violations resultieren aus verletzten Vor- oder Nachbedingungen, Programmierfehlern oder korrumpierten Speicherzuständen des Frameworks. Bei einer Violation bricht das System die Ausführung sofort und unumkehrbar über <code>ara::core::Abort()</code> ab <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00090\">[SWS_CORE_00090]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12404\">[SWS_CORE_12404]</a>. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Einordnung & Zweck</h4>
<p>Das Modul <code>ara::core</code> ist die grundlegende Basisbibliothek der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform und wird in der offiziellen Spezifikation <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#page=60">AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf (R25-11)</a> definiert. Es stellt den fehlerlosen Rückgabetyp <code>ara::core::Result</code> sowie die Fehlerdomänen-Basisklasse <code>ara::core::ErrorDomain</code> bereit, welche den Kontext für eine Menge von Fehlerbedingungen definiert; ErrorDomain-Subklassen sind die Wurzel aller Fehlerdaten <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_10303">[SWS_CORE_10303]</a>. Fehlerbehandlung erfolgt in der Adaptive Platform grundsätzlich ohne C++-Exceptions über <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> und <code>ara::core::Result</code> nach dem „ValueOrError“-Konzept (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>). Der Namespace <code>ara</code> und alle darunterliegenden Namespaces sind zudem von AUTOSAR reserviert; fügt eine Adaptive Application dort eigene Deklarationen hinzu, ist das Verhalten undefiniert (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>). Damit bildet <code>ara::core</code> das gemeinsame Fundament für Initialisierung, Fehlerbehandlung und Nebenläufigkeitsregeln aller AP-Funktionscluster.</p>
<h4>Zentrale Objekte und typische Verwendung</h4>
<p><code>ara::core::Result<T, E></code> enthält entweder einen Wert oder einen Fehler; der Fehlertyp muss <code>ErrorCode</code> sein, sonst liegt ein Compile-Fehler vor <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html">[SWS_CORE_00701]</a>, mit Spezialisierungen für Referenztypen <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_T_E_8b59ba.html">[SWS_CORE_00901]</a> und für <code>void</code>-Werte <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_void_E_c9d1e9.html">[SWS_CORE_00801]</a>. Erzeugt wird ein <code>Result</code> über die statischen Fabrikfunktionen <code>FromValue</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00733">[SWS_CORE_00733]</a> oder <code>FromError</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00736">[SWS_CORE_00736]</a>. <code>Bind</code> wendet ein Callable auf einen enthaltenen Wert an und liefert ein neues <code>Result</code>; enthält die Instanz keinen Wert, wird der ursprüngliche Fehler unverändert übernommen <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00768">[SWS_CORE_00768]</a>. <code>Resolve</code> liefert den Wert oder ruft im Fehlerfall ein kompatibles Callable auf <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00767">[SWS_CORE_00767]</a>, während <code>ErrorOr</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00764">[SWS_CORE_00764]</a><a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html#SWS_CORE_00763">[SWS_CORE_00763]</a> einfache Fallback-Werte liefert. <code>ErrorDomain</code>-Instanzen sind genau dann gleich, wenn ihre eindeutigen 64-Bit-Identifier übereinstimmen; der Zugriff erfolgt üblicherweise über Nicht-Member-Accessoren wie <code>GetFutureErrorDomain</code> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_10401">[SWS_CORE_10401]</a>.</p>
<p>Für Container und Textverarbeitung stellt das Modul PMR-fähige Implementierungen der C++-Standardbibliothek bereit: <code>ara::core::Vector</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Vector_53b788.html">[SWS_CORE_01301]</a>, <code>ara::core::Map</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Map_cba7f0.html">[SWS_CORE_01400]</a>, <code>ara::core::StringView</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html">[SWS_CORE_02001]</a>, <code>ara::core::BasicString</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_BasicString_b75ad8.html">[SWS_CORE_03000]</a> und <code>ara::core::Span</code> <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_Span_f16d72.html">[SWS_CORE_01900]</a>. Für Modellreferenzen auf Anwendungsebene existiert die <code>final</code>-Klasse <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> in <code>ara/core/instance_specifier.h</code>, die einen AUTOSAR-shortName-Pfad kapselt <a class="swsref vis-app" href="../classes/cl_ara_core_InstanceSpecifier_4f5967.html">[SWS_CORE_08001]</a>.</p>
<h4>Erzeugung, Lebenszyklus & Ownership</h4>
<p>Der Lebenszyklus der gesamten ARA wird zentral über die beiden freien Funktionen <code>ara::core::Initialize</code> und <code>ara::core::Deinitialize</code> gesteuert. <code>Initialize</code> startet das ARA-Framework; dies kann die Initialisierung interner Datenstrukturen und Systemressourcen sowie das Starten von Hintergrund-Threads umfassen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15003">[SWS_CORE_15003]</a>. Nutzt <code>Initialize</code> die Injektion von Kommandozeilenargumenten, müssen die betreffenden Argumente transparent entfernt werden, damit das Argument-Parsing der Applikation nicht beeinflusst wird <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15006">[SWS_CORE_15006]</a>. Ein erfolgreicher Aufruf versetzt das Framework in einen Zustand, in dem alle konfigurierten Komponenten sofort API-Aufrufe bedienen können <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90026">[SWS_CORE_90026]</a>; ein zweiter Aufruf ohne vorheriges <code>Deinitialize</code> liefert <code>kAlreadyInitialized</code>, ohne die laufende Instanz zu stören <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90029">[SWS_CORE_90029]</a>. <code>Deinitialize</code> startet umgekehrt das Herunterfahren des Frameworks, einschließlich Beendigung gestarteter Hintergrund-Threads und Freigabe dynamischen Speichers sowie weiterer Systemressourcen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15004">[SWS_CORE_15004]</a>; ist das Framework nicht erfolgreich initialisiert oder bereits deinitialisiert, liefert jeder Aufruf <code>kNotInitialized</code> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90030">[SWS_CORE_90030]</a>.</p>
<p>Nur eine kleine, explizit benannte Teilmenge von <code>ara::core</code> – u. a. <code>ErrorCode</code>, <code>StringView</code>, <code>Result</code> (ohne <code>ValueOrThrow</code>), <code>ErrorDomain</code> (ohne <code>ThrowAsException</code>), <code>Initialize</code>, <code>Abort</code>, <code>SetAbortHandler</code> und <code>AddAbortHandler</code> – darf unabhängig von <code>Initialize</code>/<code>Deinitialize</code> benutzt werden <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15002">[SWS_CORE_15002]</a>. Das Verhalten aller anderen ARA-Funktionen vor <code>Initialize</code> ist implementierungsdefiniert <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_15005">[SWS_CORE_15005]</a>, und auch ein Aufruf nach <code>Deinitialize</code> außerhalb dieser Teilmenge hat implementierungsdefiniertes Verhalten, da ein entsprechender Laufzeitcheck aus Performancegründen bewusst nicht gefordert wurde <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90022">[SWS_CORE_90022]</a>. Die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">Guidelines for using Adaptive Platform interfaces</a> fassen dies als verbindlichen Startup/Shutdown-Vertrag: <code>Initialize</code> ist am Einsprungpunkt aufzurufen, <code>Deinitialize</code> erst nachdem alle ARA-Ressourcen auch in anderen Threads freigegeben wurden; beide liefern <code>Result<void></code>, das geprüft werden muss, und ein Fehler ist nicht behebbar, sodass die Applikation mit <code>EXIT_FAILURE</code> terminieren muss (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>). Ergänzend untersagt die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a> clusterspezifische Initialisierungsfunktionen: Benötigt ein Funktionscluster explizite Initialisierung oder Deinitialisierung, muss er ausschließlich <code>ara::core::Initialize</code>/<code>ara::core::Deinitialize</code> nutzen.</p>
<h4>Fehlerbehandlung, Nebenläufigkeit & Einschränkungen</h4>
<p>Die Spezifikation definiert Thread-Safety präzise: Eine nicht-statische AUTOSAR-API-Memberfunktion ist thread-safe, wenn sie ohne Synchronisation durch den Aufrufer gleichzeitig auf demselben Objekt aus mehreren Threads aufgerufen werden darf; Destruktoren und Zuweisungsoperatoren sind üblicherweise nicht thread-safe <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13200">[SWS_CORE_13200]</a>. Wird eine nicht-thread-safe Memberfunktion dennoch konkurrierend auf demselben Objekt aufgerufen, ist das Verhalten undefiniert – selbst wenn die andere beteiligte Funktion thread-safe ist <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13203">[SWS_CORE_13203]</a>; ohne Synchronisation zulässig ist dagegen der konkurrierende Aufruf auf unterschiedlichen Instanzen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13205">[SWS_CORE_13205]</a>. Als non-thread-safe spezifizierte Callbacks bzw. rein virtuelle Funktionen ruft die ARA-Implementierung ausschließlich sequenziell auf, etwa <code>ara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseNotifier</code>, während z. B. <code>ara::phm::RecoveryAction::RecoveryHandler</code> thread-safe ist <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13214">[SWS_CORE_13214]</a>. Die Nutzung beliebiger ARA-APIs innerhalb eines Signal-Handlers führt zu undefiniertem Verhalten, sofern nicht anders spezifiziert <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_13210">[SWS_CORE_13210]</a> (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>: Async-Signal-Safety). Zusätzlich verlangt die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a>, dass jede API-Funktion ihren Thread-Safety-Level als „thread-safe“, „not thread-safe“ oder „conditional“ angibt, und dass der Thread-Safety-Vertrag bidirektional gilt: Ist eine API thread-safe spezifiziert, muss auch die vom Vendor oder Nutzer bereitgestellte Implementierung, etwa Callbacks oder rein virtuelle Skeleton-Funktionen, diese Zusage einhalten (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>).</p>
<p>Für nicht behebbare Fehler unterscheidet <code>ara::core</code> die Violation von der regulären Fehlerbehandlung: Eine Violation ist die Folge verletzter Vor- oder Nachbedingungen des Frameworks und nicht behebbar, vergleichbar einer fehlgeschlagenen Assertion <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00021">[SWS_CORE_00021]</a>. Bei einer standardisierten Violation wird der Prozess über <code>ara::core::Abort</code> abnormal beendet; eine Debug-Meldung gemäß der DLT-Definition wird auf <code>stderr</code> ausgegeben und soll mit der Context ID des erkennenden Funktionsclusters in die Log-Sinks geschrieben werden <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00090">[SWS_CORE_00090]</a>. Während ein Aufruf von <code>Abort</code> läuft, blockieren weitere Aufrufe die aufrufenden Threads <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12407">[SWS_CORE_12407]</a>; installierte Abort-Handler werden dabei in umgekehrter Installationsreihenfolge aufgerufen, ohne Handler wird <code>std::abort()</code> aufgerufen <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_12404">[SWS_CORE_12404]</a>. Diese Trennung von über <code>Result</code>/<code>ErrorCode</code> behebbaren Fehlern und nicht behebbaren Violations <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00021">[SWS_CORE_00021]</a> wird von der <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a> als genereller Grundsatz für alle AP-Funktionscluster gestützt.</p>
<h4>Integration & Konfiguration</h4>
<p>Jeder ARA-Funktionscluster nutzt beim Logging über <code>ara::log</code> die standardisierten Log-and-Trace-Einstellungen aus <code>ara::core</code>, insbesondere Context ID und Message-ID-Bereich <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_00055">[SWS_CORE_00055]</a>. Dazu definiert die Spezifikation standardisierte Log-Kontext-IDs je Funktionscluster, u. a. <code>#COM</code> für com, <code>#COR</code> für core, <code>#CRY</code> für crypto, <code>#DIA</code> für diag, <code>#EXE</code> für exec, <code>#LOG</code> für log und <code>#PER</code> für per <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_90024">[SWS_CORE_90024]</a>. Auf Anforderungsebene ergänzt die <a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#page=23">AUTOSAR AP RS General</a>, dass ARA-Interfaces <code>ara::core</code>-Typen anstelle der C++-Standardtypen verwenden müssen, sofern <code>ara::core</code> einen äquivalenten Typ bereitstellt. Da der Namespace <code>ara</code> vollständig für AUTOSAR reserviert ist, stehen alle Datentypen eines Funktionsclusters zusätzlich über eine Forwarding-Header-Datei <code><fc>_fwd.h</code> zur Verfügung (<a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">EXP InterfacesGuidelines</a>).</p>

<li><a href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_InterfacesGuidelines.pdf#page=9">AUTOSAR AP EXP InterfacesGuidelines (R25-11)</a> – Startup/Shutdown-Vertrag, Fehlerbehandlungskonzept, Thread- und Signal-Safety-Grundsätze.</li>

</ul><h4>Architekturkontext: gemeinsame Vertrags- und Laufzeittypen</h4><p>Die Core Types bündeln gemeinsame Klassen und Funktionalität für die öffentlichen Schnittstellen mehrerer Functional Clusters. <code>Result</code> und <code>Future</code> tragen rückgewinnbare Fehler als Rückgabewert, während <code>Initialize()</code> und <code>Deinitialize()</code> den gemeinsamen ARA-Lebenszyklus einordnen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign.pdf#nameddest=section.18.1">EXP PlatformDesign §18.1 „Error Handling“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.1.2">RS General §4.1.2 „Error handling“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign.pdf#nameddest=section.18.4">EXP PlatformDesign §18.4 „Global initialization and shutdown functions“</a></p><p>Die in <code>ara::core</code> bereitgestellten Container und View-Typen adressieren zudem die für Automotive-Anwendungen ungeeignete Speicherallokation mancher Standardbibliothekstypen; <code>StringView</code>, <code>Span</code>, <code>Optional</code> und <code>Variant</code> unterstützen außerdem Manifest-bezogene API-Konstrukte. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign.pdf#nameddest=section.18.2">EXP PlatformDesign §18.2 „Advanced data types“</a></p><h4>Kapitel-7-Vertrag zwischen Anwendung und Functional Clustern</h4><p>Core definiert den gemeinsamen Rahmen für alle Functional Clusters: <code>Initialize()</code> und <code>Deinitialize()</code> können weitere Cluster nach Implementierungsbedarf initialisieren bzw. deinitialisieren;
